chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Sa'd al-Askaf, from Ziyad ibn 'Isa, from Abu'l-Jarud, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali (peace be upon him), that he used to say:

Whoever frequents the mosques will gain one of eight things: a brother who will assist him for Allah's sake, or valuable knowledge, or a firm sign (a clear verse), or an awaited mercy, or a word that will guide him away from ruin, or he will hear a word that will lead him to guidance, or he will abandon a sin out of fear (of God), or out of modesty.

key_terms.آيَةً مُحْكَمَةً: a firm/clear sign — an unambiguous Quranic verse or divine guidance
key_terms.اخْتَلَفَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ: frequents the mosque — regular habitual attendance, not a one-time visit
key_terms.حَيَاء: modesty/shame — a virtue of self-restraint and social conscience in Islamic ethics
key_terms.خَشْيَة: reverential fear — godly fear that motivates moral restraint

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of going to the mosque according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), as reported through a long chain of reliable narrators, emphasizes the spiritual and social benefits of regular mosque attendance. He enumerates eight distinct gains: companionship, knowledge, Quranic wisdom, divine mercy, moral correction, guidance, avoidance of sin from fear, and avoidance of sin from modesty. This teaching was addressed to the early Muslim community in Kufa, where the mosque was the center of religious, social, and educational life. The phrase 'ayatun muhkama' (a firm sign) refers to encountering a clear, unambiguous Quranic verse that strengthens one's faith.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ya`qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Ibrahim b. `Abd al-Hamid from Sa`d al-Askaf from Ziyad b. `Isa from Abi'l Jarud from al-Asbagh b. Nubata from `Ali (as). He would say:

Whoever frequents the mosques will gain one of eight things: (1) a brother who will assist him for Allah, (2) valuable knowledge, (3) a firm sign (ayatun muhkama), (4) an awaited mercy, (5) a word that will guide him away from falsehood, (6) hearing a word that will take him to guidance, (7) abandoning a sin out of humility [before Allah], or (8) modesty.
